start.text: The Wrens' old house. The boards have gone salt-grey, two are missing from the side, and every shutter is closed.
By the door an iron hook holds something round, wrapped in sailcloth and tied off at the neck with red cord. At the foot of the steps stands a three-legged iron brazier, full of grey ash.
Brother Aldous sits with his back to both of them.

told_full.text: The sailcloth is folded on the step. On the hook hangs a disc of bone-white enamel ringed in iron, an ember painted on each face: the Keepers' mark.
The same ember as the one he cut from his sleeve for you. Different hands, same pattern.
Someone has rubbed the salt off it. The paint is chipped, but the ember faces the road now.
In the brazier the ash has been raked smooth. Not lit. Raked, the way you'd make up a bed for someone expected.

told_grudging.text: The sailcloth lies in a heap under the hook. The Keepers' ember hangs bare: a disc of bone-white enamel ringed in iron, crusted with salt, its paint flaking.
Aldous hasn't cleaned it. He hasn't covered it again, either.
The brazier's ash is grey all the way down.
